 Joel Embiid (foot) is out for Sunday’s game against the Pistons. 
 Embiid said after Saturday’s win over the Bucks that he wouldn’t play Sunday, and the team has now made it official. LeBron James is not on the injury report after sitting out on Saturday, so he may see more playing time at center than he did in wins over the Knicks and Cavaliers. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Embiid producing despite availability concerns 
 Noah Rubin analyzes Joel Embiid's start to the NBA season and how his "high-level" production is a good sign with the minutes he's played, though he will sit at least one game this weekend.

 Tyrese Maxey, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Dean Wade will start Sunday’s game against the Pistons. 
 The 76ers won’t have VJ Edgecombe or Joel Embiid for Sunday’s game, resulting in two changes to the starting lineup. Caldwell-Pope will replace Edgecombe, marking his first start of the season. The other change is James, who returns after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Bucks. He’ll fill the void left by Embiid. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James (sciatica) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Pistons. 
 James is good to go after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Bucks. Dean Wade replaced him in the starting lineup, but both may start on Sunday since Joel Embiid (foot) is out. 
 Joel Embiid 
 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid accounted for 28 points (8-of-20 FGs, 12-of-14 FTs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal in Saturday’s win over the Bucks. 
 Saturday went about as well as it could have for the 76ers. LeBron James (sciatica) didn’t play, which put more on Embiid’s plate. The big man did what was expected, recording his 10th career triple-double and dominating his matchup with Milwaukee’s Myles Turner. The 76ers face the Pistons on Sunday, and Embiid won’t play. That leaves it to LeBron to shoulder a heavier workload, provided he’s cleared to play. 
 Dean Wade 
 PHI 
 Forward-Center 
 #45 
 Dean Wade (ankle) is available for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Wade is available to make his 76ers debut after missing the first two games of the season. With LeBron James (back) out, Wade will move into the starting lineup, joining Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. 
 With the 76ers as the only team with four games in Week 1, it was always unlikely that LeBron would play in all four. With Joel Embiid off the injury report Saturday, it seems like those roles could be reversed Sunday against the Pistons with Embiid sitting out and LeBron active. 
 Joel Embiid 
 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid isn’t listed on the injury report for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Embiid told reporters after the win over the Cavaliers on Thursday that he will sit out one of the 76ers’ games this weekend. Given that he’s not listed on the injury report for Saturday’s game against the Bucks, it looks like he’ll play Saturday and sit out Sunday’s game against the Pistons. Adem Bona or Jabari Walker will likely start in Embiid’s absence. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James (back) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. 
 LeBron had 17 points in the 76ers’ dramatic 29-point comeback against the Cavaliers on Thursday. With Philadelphia being the only team with four games in Week 1, it’s reasonable to assume James could sit for one of the games this weekend. The 41-year-old forward is listed as questionable for Saturday against the Bucks with a back injury. His status will have to be monitored leading up to game-time. 
 Joel Embiid 
 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid said after Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers that he will miss one of the 76ers’ final two games of the week. 
 The 76ers were the only team with a four-game Week 1, which will conclude with a Saturday-Sunday back-to-back. Embiid sitting out one game of a back-to-back, especially this early in the season, is not a surprise. The only issue is that he didn’t reveal which game he’ll miss, with the 76ers hosting Milwaukee on Saturday and Detroit on Sunday. Given the strength of those teams, the Bucks may be the team that misses out on having to deal with “The Process.” Adem Bona or Jabari Walker could get a spot start, and LeBron James may spend a little more time at center as a small-ball alternative. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James tallied 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds, five assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers. 
 James was responsible for five of the 76ers’ 14 first-half turnovers, and the offensive inefficiency led to Philadelphia falling into a 29-point hole. LeBron was much better in the second half, recording a 12/7/4/1 stat line with no turnovers. While the field-goal percentage and turnovers could be problematic at times, fantasy managers rostering James don’t have much to worry about right now. 
 Joel Embiid 
 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid accounted for 24 points (8-of-16 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers. 
 After scoring nine points on 3-of-10 shooting in the first half, Embiid shot 5-of-6 after halftime, scoring 15 points. His increased production helped the 76ers erase a 29-point deficit, as Nick Nurse’s team ramped up defensive pressure and played with more pace on offense. Embiid’s ability to keep up with his new teammates is something to watch, especially when considering his injury history. But for the most part, he’s been good through Philadelphia’s first two games.

 Anthony Black finished Sunday’s win over the Knicks with 18 points (6-of-11 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers.
 After missing the entire preseason and Orlando’s first two games with a sprained ankle, Black made his first appearance on Sunday. He was excellent, especially in the first quarter, scoring 12 points off the bench. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) likely out for 4-6 weeks and Jalen Suggs (knee) going down during the fourth quarter, Black’s return came at a great time for Orlando. Even though the Magic don’t play their next game until Wednesday, fantasy managers should add Black if he’s sitting on the waiver wire.

 RJ Barrett finished Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 20 points (9-of-21 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and three steals.
 Barrett helped keep the Raptors within striking distance of the Timberwolves in the first half, scoring 14 points. Unfortunately for him, he went cold in the third quarter, along with the rest of the Raptors, shooting 1-of-5 from the field. Toronto was outscored 35-15 as Kawhi Leonard’s absence and Scottie Barnes’ 0-of-12 shooting caught up to them. Barrett and the Raptors will look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Magic.

 Immanuel Quickley amassed 19 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 Fts), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Quickley had a productive night, but it didn’t matter much when two other Raptors starters (Scottie Barnes and Jakob Poeltl) went scoreless, shooting 0-of-14 from the field combined. IQ’s current fantasy value doesn’t align with his preseason ADP, but he’s a relatively safe bet for at least top-100 value. The Raptors play three games in Week 2, starting with the Magic on Wednesday.

 Ja’Kobe Walter accounted for 22 points (7-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Due to Kawhi Leonard’s swollen left knee, Walter was plugged into the Raptors’ starting lineup on Sunday. He was one of the few who had productive nights, shooting over 50 percent from the field and leading the Raptors in scoring. Walter’s fantasy value will hinge on who else the Raptors have available each night, most notably Leonard. But Sunday’s performance showed that he’s a worthwhile streamer when starting.

 Terrence Shannon Jr. accounted for 15 points (5-of-6 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
 The Timberwolves’ bench accounted for 41 of the team’s 117 points, led by Shannon with 15. He’s scored in double figures in all three of Minnesota’s games, but he still has work to do to become a reliable option in category leagues. Ayo Dosunmu (9/3/3 with one three-pointer) remains the better option for fantasy managers looking for value on the Timberwolves bench, even after a quiet night against the Raptors.

 Kuminga’s gotten off to a good start in Minnesota, providing consistent supplementary scoring as a starter for the Timberwolves. He won’t get many shots in a lineup headlined by Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, and Jaden McDaniels, but he’ll have enough opportunities to provide reliable value. Rostered in 56 percent of Yahoo leagues, JK has been a top-100 player in category leagues so far.

 Anthony Edwards notched 26 points (10-of-18 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), one rebound, three assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
 The Timberwolves took care of business in their home opener, with Edwards leading five double-digit scorers. After his 5-of-23 night against the Magic on Friday, fantasy managers received a nice boost in the field-goal percentage category on Sunday. Edwards didn’t record any defensive stats against the Raptors, but most managers won’t lose any sleep over it. Minnesota plays four games in Week 2, beginning with the Cavaliers on Monday.

 Kris Dunn accounted for 15 points (6-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, five steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder.
 From a fantasy standpoint, Dunn had an excellent opening week. In three games, the Clippers guard totaled 18 assists, 10 steals and four blocks, numbers that boost his value in category leagues. As of Sunday night, Dunn was rostered in just 15 percent of Yahoo leagues. The only problem with adding him now is that the Clippers don’t play again until Wednesday.

 Darius Garland tallied 16 points (7-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, 11 assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder.
 After totaling 10 assists in the Clippers’ first two games of the season, Garland recorded 11 helpers against the Thunder. That said, turnovers remain an issue, as he racked up five in the 108-101 defeat. Over three games, Garland has recorded 21 assists and 17 turnovers. So far, he’s been more valuable in eight-cat formats or to nine-cat managers willing to punt turnovers. The Clippers play three games in Week 2, starting with the Lakers on Wednesday.

 After recording two underwhelming stat lines in Oklahoma City’s first two games of the season, Hartenstein posted a double-double on Sunday. His play helped offset Chet Holmgren’s quiet night at the office (10 points, four rebounds, one steal, one block and two three-pointers), helping push Oklahoma City’s record to 3-0. Hartenstein also played 27 minutes, an encouraging number given his limited minutes last season.
